description:
Advances: ancora.derive

Severity: High (calibrated). Consolidated findings F5, F6, and the tracked F15. All three measured by the performance reviewer against Livebook as a size-comparable Elixir tree.

F5 — gate.ex:67 calls BaseView.materialize(ctx) with NO pathspecs, so the entire base tree is fetched and written to /tmp although only .spec/, test_paths and lib_paths are ever read back. On Livebook that is 698 blobs / 17.3 MiB against the 306 blobs / 2.0 MiB actually needed. Measured 6.97s cold, 495ms warm, against 227ms warm when narrowed. CI is always the cold case. One-line fix: pass pathspecs: [".spec" | preflight.config.test_paths ++ preflight.project.lib_paths] at gate.ex:67; BaseView.blobs/3 already accepts :pathspecs. While in the file, feed entry.oid to Git.read_blob/2 instead of "#{base}:#{path}", and dedupe the per-file mkdir_p! calls.
This also fixes a real disk leak: cleanup lives in a try/after that is skipped on untrapped exits (see the F26 half of the env-tier ticket). 11 leaked directories totalling 150 MB were sitting in the reviewer temp dir, several of them 24-25 MB full copies of real user projects.

F6 — compare.ex:144 rebuilds MapSet.new(ChangeSet.paths(change_set)) INSIDE changed_definition?/3, which runs once per binding per subject. Measured 33.1 microseconds per call at 294 changed paths against 0.7 hoisted, a 46x gap; at 40 subjects x 300 bindings that is 390ms of pure waste, scaling multiplicatively with diff size and corpus size. Fix: compute the MapSet once per run and thread it in, or add a path_set field to %ChangeSet{} populated in compute/1.

F15 (was tracked; folded here because its fix shape depends on the same call path) — extract.ex:17 runs Code.string_to_quoted over a whole source file per binding, on both sides, with no memoization (compare.ex:121-122). Livebook largest module costs 8.43ms per parse, so 50 bound functions in one changed 82 KiB file is 843ms for a single subject. Verified with :erlang.trace_pattern :call_count that 122 of 247 Code.string_to_quoted calls in a real gate run are re-parses of a file an earlier stage already parsed.

Important scoping note: ancora-u38 (the on-disk OID cache) does NOT cover any of this. The perf reviewer measured the blob-fetch term at 405ms for a whole 698-file tree and 211ms narrowed, while the writes in that same stage cost 495ms warm and the redundant parsing costs hundreds more. The cost here is tokenizing bytes already in memory, which no blob cache touches. Every fix above is in-run and in-memory and needs no ADR change, whereas the cache reopens no_execution_no_state. Land this first and re-measure before deciding the cache is still worth the charter cost.

Sequencing: ready now. The ancora-xla.9 memo ruling is DELETE, so F15 is a plain per-run parse result threaded through Compare as an argument; no memo, no ETS. ancora-u38 is deferred out of the epic and waits on this ticket for Manuel's post-merge Atlas bench.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: tagged tests under ancora.derive and ancora.gate: test/ancora/base_view_test.exs (pathspec-narrowed materialize; oid-based read_blob; one mkdir_p per directory), test/ancora/derive/compare_test.exs and test/ancora/derive/change_set_test.exs (hoisted path set), test/ancora/derive/extract_test.exs or pipeline_test.exs (parse count), test/ancora/gate_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) gate.ex materializes only .spec plus test_paths plus lib_paths, asserted by a test listing the materialized tree; (2) the changed-path MapSet is built once per run; (3) each source file is parsed at most once per side per run, asserted by a counter or trace, not by timing; (4) before/after numbers on Livebook or a size-comparable tree posted in the IMPLEMENTED comment; (5) temp dirs are cleaned on the raising-resolver path (shares a fixture with ancora-xla.2)
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: the base tree materialization is narrowed to the paths the gate reads, and each source file is parsed once per side.

The worker was right and it stopped before touching anything. SCOPE IS NARROW: teach read_blob/2 to accept an already-resolved blob OID without rewriting it to <base>:<path>. Both clauses (batch port and git show fallback) may change. Do NOT touch Git.run/3's option handling, the ls-tree parser, or pathspec_args/1.
  OVERLAP WARNING: ancora-xla.8 has an unmerged commit editing the SAME read_blob/2 fallback clause, adding stderr_to_stdout: false to its run/3 call. It will very likely merge first. Keep that option intact if you see it, and expect a rebase either way; whichever lands second gets a cold rebase worker.)

Every ticket here is required to edit a spec, so this finding is structurally guaranteed and the decision-record edit is forced rather than optional. Write a real contract statement describing what you actually built; do NOT add a hollow line to silence the finding, which a grader will read as finding-silencing and bounce.)

Needed touch: lib/ancora/git.ex
Reason: BaseView must pass each ls-tree entry OID to Git.read_blob/2, but Git.read_blob/2 currently treats every binary as a path and rewrites it to <base>:<path>. Passing entry.oid from an allowed file would therefore request <base>:<oid> and fail. The smallest correct change teaches Git.read_blob/2 to accept an OID without rewriting it; no currently allowed file can provide that behavior while preserving the base_reads_batched contract.
Evidence: git show <blob-oid> succeeds in this worktree, while git show <blob-oid>: exits 128. No implementation files have been changed.

SCOPE_EXPANSION GRANTED (orchestrator, 2026-09-03). lib/ancora/git.ex and test/ancora/git_test.exs are now in Allowed touches, narrowly: read_blob/2 learns to accept an already-resolved blob OID without rewriting it. The request was correct and it stopped before changing anything, which is the behaviour I want. The fault is mine: this ticket's own text ordered the oid-based read while withholding the only file that can provide it. Fourth instance of the same admission defect in this epic. One thing the expansion request could not have known: ancora-xla.8 has an unmerged commit editing the same read_blob/2 fallback clause. See the widened Allowed touches for the handling.

BLOCKING 1 - the parse-once claim is proven for Compare, never for a gate run. test/ancora/derive/compare_test.exs:231 traces Ancora.Derive.Extract.parse/2, calls Compare.prepare_sources by hand over a duplicated subject pair, then calls Compare.compare twice with parsed_sources passed in explicitly, and asserts two parse calls and no third. That proves Compare does not re-parse when it is handed a map. It does not prove the gate builds that map once. Compare.compare at lib/ancora/derive/compare.ex:30 resolves :parsed_sources through Keyword.get_lazy, so deleting `parsed_sources: parsed_sources` at lib/ancora/gate.ex:171, or deleting the prepare_sources call at lib/ancora/gate.ex:156-157 outright, restores per-subject re-preparation and leaves every test in this diff green. F15 is the ticket's largest measured win (111.869 ms to 3.019 ms) and its production wiring has no test. The spec scenario this change added, ancora.derive.scenario.extraction_parses_once_per_side, states "when the gate compares both subjects"; nothing drives the gate. Ticket verification item 3 says "per run", not per Compare call. gate_test.exs already carries start_trace_forwarder/1 at line 514: build a corpus with two subjects binding definitions in one changed lib file, trace Extract.parse/2 across Gate.check, and assert exactly one base call and one head call.

BLOCKING 2 - both count assertions drain the trace mailbox with `after 0` and can silently under-count. test/ancora/base_view_test.exs:149 and test/ancora/gate_test.exs:504 both drain with a zero timeout. Trace delivery to the tracer is asynchronous with respect to the tracee, which is why :erlang.trace_delivered/1 exists, and the forwarder process adds a second unordered hop before the message reaches the test. base_view_test.exs:115 asserts the mkdir count for temp/lib equals 1; restoring the per-file File.mkdir_p! produces 2 calls, and a drain that caught only the first still passes. gate_test.exs:214 refutes membership of the notes/private.txt OID; a drain that stops before that read is forwarded passes even when the whole tree is materialized again. Both failure modes are silent green on exactly the regressions the tests exist to catch, and the base_view case is the tighter window because only Path.wildcard separates materialize from the drain. Fix: call :erlang.trace_delivered(traced), wait for {:trace_delivered, traced, ref}, then send the forwarder a synchronous ping and wait for its reply before draining. Setting the tracer to the test process itself removes the second hop and makes trace_delivered sufficient on its own.

WARNING - the narrowing test never uses a non-default path configuration. test/ancora/gate_test.exs:180 is named "gate materializes only specs, tests, and configured library paths" but writes a stock lib/ and test/ layout, so replacing the expression at lib/ancora/gate.ex:73 with a literal [".spec", "test", "lib"] survives. The configured-path plumbing is the half most likely to break on a real umbrella or src/ project. gate_test.exs:111 already shows the fixture shape for a config.yml with lib_paths: src.

WARNING - the cleanup test does not exercise the try/after it appears to guard. test/ancora/gate_test.exs:219 is titled "when a resolver callback raises", but lib/ancora/derive.ex:123 rescues that raise into {:error, {:resolver_exception, ...}}, so assemble returns normally, the after at lib/ancora/gate.ex:77 fires on the ordinary return, and the raise the test asserts on comes from gate_error outside the try. Replacing the try/after with a plain File.rm_rf after assemble keeps the test green. It does satisfy ticket item 5 as written and the assertion itself is good: it captures the exact temp root from a return_trace on BaseView.materialize/3 and refutes that path, which beats counting temp directories. Just do not read it as exception-safety coverage.

WARNING - inconsistent async treatment of the same global hazard. base_view_test.exs:4 and compare_test.exs:2 were both flipped from async: true to async: false because :erlang.trace_pattern is VM-wide, yet gate_test.exs inherits async: true from Ancora.TestCase while installing global patterns on Git.read_blob/2 and on BaseView.materialize/3 with a return_trace match spec. No message cross-talk is possible today because only the test pid carries the :call flag, but if any other async module ever traces Git.read_blob/2 the two on_exit disables race and the loser drains nothing, which compounds with Blocking 2 into a false green.

RECOMMENDATION - base_view_test.exs:23 asserts {:read_blob, "entry.oid"} by comparing Macro.to_string of the argument expression in production source. Destructuring the OID into a local, or renaming entry, breaks it with byte-identical behaviour. gate_test.exs:213 already proves OID-based reads behaviourally by asserting the read arguments are the rev-parse OIDs, so the AST assertion is redundant coupling on top of a real test.

RECOMMENDATION - git_test.exs:108 covers only the batch: false fallback clause. The batch-port clause of Git.read_blob/2 also changed from blob_spec/2 to read_spec/2 and is exercised only incidentally through Gate.check. A direct RunContext with the port open and a resolved OID would pin it, and would catch a regex or clause-ordering change in read_spec/2 that only affects the port path.

Good work worth keeping: compare_test.exs:285 is the strongest test in the diff. It builds a ChangeSet whose entries name lib/not-billing.ex while path_set names lib/billing.ex and asserts the drift finding follows path_set, which proves the hoist by divergence rather than by restating it. By comparison change_set_test.exs:40 derives both sides of its equality from the same struct and only catches path_set being left at the empty default. git_test.exs:108 is behavioural and would fail loudly on the <base>:<oid> rewrite, which is the right shape for the SCOPE_EXPANSION grant.

That is adjacent behavior, not the literal contract, and F15 is this ticket's headline claim. A gate-level Extract.parse/2 trace over a Gate.check run whose diff touches a bound source file would close it.

  docs/spec and no .spec at all, so the gate requirement as written is now false, and
  the test this same commit added at gate_test.exs:226 is a passing tagged test that
  violates it. Two must requirements now state different rules for one behavior, which
  is the exact ancora-v1n failure the ticket's Allowed-touches note was written to
  prevent, and .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md is already in Allowed touches for
  substantive edits. One-line fix: mirror the derive wording.

Notes:
- prepare_base_dirs/3's spec-dir parameterization is correct but untested. M1b survives
  the whole of gate_test.exs. The behavior it protects is reachable: with the mutation,
  mix spec.check --root <fixture> --base <commit predating docs/spec> --spec-dir
  docs/spec raises the same index.ex:74 RuntimeError, and HEAD returns result=pass.
  A fixture whose base commit lacks the configured spec dir would close it.
- --spec-dir is still not honored end to end. Ancora.Gate.Preflight.corpus/1 at
  lib/ancora/gate/preflight.ex:57-62 hardcodes File.dir?(root <> "/.spec") and returns
  the env error "no .spec/ directory in <root>; run mix spec.init" regardless of
  --spec-dir. A project whose specs live only under docs/spec cannot start a gate run
  without an empty .spec/ directory sitting there, which is why the new test writes
  .spec/.keep after committing and why my repro fixture needed the same. Pre-existing,
  outside this ticket's ordered items, and out of its Allowed touches.
- test/ancora/base_view_test.exs:149 still drains with `after 0` and got no sync_traces
  treatment; only the two gate_test.exs call sites did. Consistent with the auditor not
  upholding the critic's second blocking finding. Flake risk, not silent-green risk.
- The ticket text still lists `.spec/decisions/**` under both Allowed touches and Out of
  Scope (files), and Out of Scope (intent) still says "no ADR change" while the body and
  work-order item 5 both mandate one. Already flagged by the auditor; repeating it so
  the next reader does not have to adjudicate it a third time.
